about: Published from the deck library export by scripts/build_archetypes.py. Read by gates P10, P13, P15 and by scripts/find.py. Families are visual; budgets are words on glass per kit canvas.
library: optional, for re-mining only: DECK_LIBRARY, else paths.LIB_DEFAULT

cover.name: Cover
cover.definition: Opens the deck: names the engagement, the parties and the date in one title stack set against an image field, a brand panel or a welcome row of the people attending.

agenda.name: Agenda
agenda.definition: Lists the parts of the session or document once, in order, as numbered rows, bars or tiles, so the audience holds the whole route before it starts.

section-divider.name: Section divider
section-divider.definition: Marks the turn into a new part with a numeral, a part name and one graphic anchor, and almost no other words. Dividers in one deck share one frame and advance only the number.

closing.name: Closing
closing.definition: Ends the deck with one last line: a sign-off with contact detail, an attributed testimonial beside it, or a single closing claim, and no new argument.

problem-framing.name: Problem framing
problem-framing.definition: Makes the audience accept the problem before any answer: the situation, its pressures or its causes as parallel headed columns or cards, often over a shared band of consequences or figures.

principles.name: Principles
principles.definition: States the beliefs or design decisions that govern the solution as numbered peer cards, each with a short rationale, so the audience agrees with how the work will be done.

why-us.name: Why us
why-us.definition: Names the few reasons to choose the vendor as numbered pillars or panels, each backed by a short proof, so the audience can repeat the reasons afterwards.

offering-pillars.name: Offering pillars
offering-pillars.definition: Shows what the offer is made of as two to five peer panels, tiers or bands, each naming one part the client would buy and what it brings.

catalogue.name: Catalogue
catalogue.definition: Lists every agent, product or accelerator on offer as uniform entries carrying the same fields, such as name, type, purpose and a link, so the audience can scan the full set.

team-roster.name: Team roster
team-roster.definition: Introduces the people who will do the work: portraits with name and role in a row or grid, or one profile page per lead with a sectioned biography.

case-wall.name: Case wall
case-wall.definition: Shows several delivered engagements at once, each reduced to a headline and an outcome figure, so the breadth of proof reads at a glance.

the-ask.name: The ask
the-ask.definition: States the decisions the audience is asked to make now, one verb-led card each, and the dated milestones that follow, so the meeting ends in a commitment.

process-flow.name: Process flow
process-flow.definition: Shows how the proposed solution runs, step by step in reading order, with what happens and what is checked at each step, so the audience believes it works end to end.

as-is-process.name: As-is process
as-is-process.definition: Walks today's process stage by stage and pins each pain to the stage where it occurs, so the audience sees where the work breaks before any fix is shown.

input-process-output.name: Input, process, output
input-process-output.definition: Frames the mechanism as three panels read left to right: what goes in, the numbered method in the widest middle panel, and what comes out.

decision-logic.name: Decision logic
decision-logic.definition: Shows the rules that route each case to an action, a ladder of yes or no questions or a split into disposition lanes, so the audience sees the system decides predictably and can be audited.

swimlane-handoff.name: Swimlane hand-off
swimlane-handoff.definition: Separates actors into lanes under shared stage headers and draws every hand-off between them, so the audience sees who acts when and where people stay in control.

worked-example.name: Worked example
worked-example.definition: Proves the mechanism on one named instance, a record, a case or a persona, traced hop by hop with its literal values, payloads or outcomes, so a technical reader can check rather than trust.

engagement-model.name: Engagement model
engagement-model.definition: Shows how the vendor will run the engagement: the method steps or workstreams, with the activities, inputs and deliverables of each, so the audience trusts the way of working.

layered-architecture.name: Layered architecture
layered-architecture.definition: Stacks the platform as full-width layers from sources to consumers, each naming what it holds, so the audience sees every part has a place and depends on the one beneath.

solution-architecture.name: Solution architecture
solution-architecture.definition: Places the components in tab-headed zones inside a drawn boundary, sources outside one edge, consumers outside the other and a platform band beneath, so every crossing reads as a deliberate decision.

governance-model.name: Governance model
governance-model.definition: Sets out the forums, cadences and escalation path of the joint engagement as tiers read top to bottom, keyed across to who attends and what each decides.

from-to-shift.name: From-to shift
from-to-shift.definition: Draws the current state and the target state of the same subject side by side or stacked, with the change carried by a wedge, a bridge or paired rows, so the shift itself is the message.

options-comparison.name: Options comparison
options-comparison.definition: Sets two or more alternatives against the same criteria or on one shared axis, with the recommended one marked, so the audience sees why it wins.

gap-analysis.name: Gap analysis
gap-analysis.definition: Sets what exists against what is missing, or the visible symptom against the hidden cause, in opposed zones, so the audience sees the gap the proposal fills.

case-study.name: Case study
case-study.definition: Tells one delivered engagement on one page in a fixed order: the context and need, what was built as a small flow or stack, and the reported outcomes in a solid figure rail.

deep-dive.name: Deep dive with brief rail
deep-dive.definition: Explains one use case, method or mechanism on one page: a wide zone holds its diagram or exhibit, and a narrow rail restates the problem, the approach and the decision it supports.

executive-summary.name: Executive summary
executive-summary.definition: Compresses the whole proposal onto one page partitioned into labelled cells, the ask, the answer, the scope, the figures and the assumptions, so a reader who sees nothing else can agree to it.

scope-and-assumptions.name: Scope and assumptions
scope-and-assumptions.definition: Fences the commitment: what is in and what is out set against each other, with the assumptions and dependencies it rests on, so nothing is promised by omission.

use-case-map.name: Use-case map
use-case-map.definition: Places many use cases or agents on the client's value chain, functions or phases, so the audience sees coverage and where each one acts.

coverage-matrix.name: Coverage matrix
coverage-matrix.definition: Crosses two lists, such as owners by duties, phases by domains or stages by terms, so every cell states what applies where.

prioritization-matrix.name: Prioritization matrix
prioritization-matrix.definition: Scores or plots many candidates against criteria or on two axes such as value and effort, so the audience can agree which go first.

reference-table.name: Reference table
reference-table.definition: Lists many items as rows against the same attribute columns, a catalogue, a method map or a value breakdown, so a reader can look up and compare any row.

hub-and-spoke.name: Hub and spoke
hub-and-spoke.definition: Puts one core at the centre, a platform, a team or an idea, with its parts arranged around it by spokes, petals, quadrant tiles or rings, so the audience sees what everything depends on.

lifecycle-loop.name: Lifecycle loop
lifecycle-loop.definition: Places stages on a closed loop around a hub or an open centre, with directional arrows, so the work reads as repeating and improving rather than ending.

convergence-hub.name: Convergence hub
convergence-hub.definition: Draws many feeders, sources or cases converging by arrows onto one shared element, a disc, a card or a band, which then reads out to outcomes, so everything visibly resolves into one contract or implication.

gantt.name: Gantt
gantt.definition: Places workstreams as bars on a dated grid of weeks, months or quarters, with milestones and gate lines crossing it, so the audience sees duration, overlap and the critical dates.

phased-roadmap.name: Phased roadmap
phased-roadmap.definition: Breaks delivery into a few phases or waves in time order under a milestone rail or arrow, each repeating one anatomy of scope, deliverables, exit gate and duration.

value-horizons.name: Value horizons
value-horizons.definition: Shows value, capability or a relationship growing across years or horizons, as year headers over a rising curve, a road or columns that grow denser, so the audience sees the climb and the destination.

maturity-model.name: Maturity model
maturity-model.definition: Ranks levels of capability or autonomy from basic to advanced as a staircase, tapering wedge, graded ladder or positioned curve, so the audience places itself on a rung and sees the next one.

headline-figures.name: Headline figures
headline-figures.definition: Makes three to six large figures the argument, a finding, a result or the size of the prize, each explained, decomposed into drivers or sourced in the cards beneath.

commercials.name: Commercials
commercials.definition: Presents the price and what it buys: a price panel or rail beside blocks for scope, team, duration and terms, or a cost table resolving into the price, so the audience can approve the spend.

credentials.name: Credentials
credentials.definition: Shows the firm in facts: scale figures, reach, recognition and sector breadth, stacked as a stat band over a split of the workforce, a map, badges or marks.

product-screen.name: Product screen
product-screen.definition: Lets the running product carry the claim: one framed screen, a device mockup on a band or numbered screen tiles in tour order, with a title and almost no other words.

output-capture.name: Output capture
output-capture.definition: Reproduces a real deliverable the solution produced, a table, a chart page, a letter or a dashboard, whole as a captured page, so the reader can inspect actual output.
